note: Draft, not in the tool. Rules Adam gave on Nov 17, 2026 for the ranked Add product list: a client does not go back to an older product once it owns the newer one that does the same job. Each rule only stops a suggestion. It never removes a product from a canvas, and Create your own play stays freeform. Product ids are the tool's own (canvas/catalog.json).
principle: Any newer product that offers the same functionality as an older product: the client is not going to go backwards. (Adam, Nov 17)

rules.adam: I would never offer somebody Adobe Analytics who already owned Customer Journey Analytics.
rules.one_way: A client with Adobe Analytics can still be offered Customer Journey Analytics.
rules.tool_today: No goal calls for Adobe Analytics. The connection aa-cja carries two services (report suite data in CJA, migration to CJA), which fit the forward direction. The Coworker + Customer Journey Analytics service 'Adobe Analytics and CJA data validation and fixes' needs Adobe Analytics on the canvas and shows an 'Add Adobe Analytics' button on Create your own play. Today's Add product menu on Create your own play lists Adobe Analytics first when Customer Journey Analytics is on the canvas; Adam decided on Nov 17 that the rule applies there too.

rules.adam: If someone owns Journey Optimizer, they're not going to buy Target.
rules.tool_today: To settle with Adam: the tool documents a native connection ajo-target with the service 'Journey Optimizer offers in Target tests' (XA07), and two first-page chips add Target to a Journey Optimizer setup: 'My client wants to test store content' (abandoned-carts) and 'My client wants to start testing too' (cant-see-what-works).
rules.status: Set. Adam, Nov 17: "I know a lot of people that have Target have upgraded to journey optimizer and have kept it so that's fine. You could leave that one as is." Read as: the tool keeps pairing the two for clients who own both (the connection, its service and the two first-page chips stay), and the rule only stops Target being suggested once Journey Optimizer is on the canvas. This reading was put to Adam; change it if he corrects it.

rules.adam: If someone owns Adobe Experience Manager cloud service or Edge Delivery or even Sites Optimizer I don't think they're going to buy AEM Sites. Nov 17, later, asked which AEM Sites: "if they own edge delivery services they probably do not want to go backwards to traditional AEM publish."
rules.tool_today: To settle with Adam: the tool has three AEM products: 'AEM Sites' (its texts describe AEM Sites as a Cloud Service), 'AEM Sites with Edge Delivery Services' and 'Sites Optimizer'. It documents native connections aemsites-eds (five services, AEM authoring as the Edge Delivery content source) and aemsites-so (four services), and several first-page chips say the client already owns AEM Sites. How the customer data names the AEM products decides the mapping. On Create your own play the menu offers AEM Sites two ways: 'With Edge Delivery Services' (eds) and 'With traditional AEM Publish' (aemsites).
rules.status: Set by Adam: once AEM Sites with Edge Delivery Services is on the canvas, never suggest AEM Sites with traditional AEM Publish (the tool's product 'aemsites'). Sites Optimizer alone does not trigger it. The tool keeps the aemsites-eds connection and its five services for clients who own both, and the first-page chips that say a client already owns AEM Sites are untouched. In the ranked list the two AEM Sites deliveries already share one row, so the rule mostly shows on Create your own play, where the AEM Sites entry offers both.

not_in_the_tool.adam: If someone owns Journey Optimizer or Marketo, they are not going to purchase Adobe Campaign. We are phasing Adobe Campaign out.
not_in_the_tool.effect: Adobe Campaign is not a product in the tool (left out on Nov 10), so the list can never suggest it. When the customer data is read, Campaign is not a candidate.

not_in_the_tool.adam: If someone owns Adobe Commerce cloud service or Adobe Commerce Optimizer they're not going to then purchase Adobe Commerce on prem.
not_in_the_tool.effect: The tool has one product, 'Adobe Commerce', and no on-premises product, so the list can never suggest it. When the customer data is read, ask Adam whether on-premises owners count as owning Adobe Commerce.

where_the_rules_apply.adam: I would say not Adobe analytics first because they'd be going backwards.
where_the_rules_apply.decision: The rules apply to the ranked Add product list on ready-made plays and to the Add product menu on Create your own play. On Create your own play the product leaves 'Connects to your canvas' and sits on a 'Not suggested' line, where a partner can still add it.

no_rule.adam: Marketo and Journey Optimizer, especially Journey Optimizer B2B, need each other. I was wrong with that.
no_rule.effect: No hold-back between Marketo Engage and Journey Optimizer or Journey Optimizer B2B Edition. Keep suggesting them.
